sg.title: Nintendo Teases Upcoming LEGO Yoshi Set
sg.description: Summary Nintendo and LEGO have confirmed a new Super Mario Yoshi set designed for adult collectorsTeased on the Nintendo Today app the upcoming build features a large-scale sculpted recreation of Yoshi's faceOfficial piece counts pricing and launch timing remain unannounced ahead of an indicated 2027 arrival Toy manufacturing giant LEGO and gaming company Nintendo have officially announced an upcoming LEGO Super Mario Yoshi set designed specifically for adult collectors. First teased via the Nintendo Today mobile application with the tagline "New Lego Super Mario Set Hatching Soon," the forthcoming release expands the collaborative catalog with a detailed brick-built recreation of the iconic green dinosaur. Belonging to LEGO's dedicated "Adults Welcome" collection, the initial teaser imagery provides a tight crop of Yoshi's face, displaying brick-sculpted eyes, rounded cheeks, and an oversized nose. The visible geometry points toward a significantly larger, display-oriented model in comparison to the smaller interactive figures standard to the mainline Super Mario range. While details remain unconfirmed regarding whether the character will arrive as an independent statue or alongside an accessory like a personal kart, the release joins adult-targeted Nintendo centerpieces such as the Mighty Bowser and Piranha Plant builds. The upcoming set represents Yoshi's first major adult release since 2024's 1,215-piece Super Mario World: Mario & Yoshi pixel-art homage. While LEGO and Nintendo have not confirmed the official pricing, piece count, or launch date, a 2027 copyright notice visible on the teaser suggests a release within the coming year. sg.title: UN Global Compact Calls for Faster Climate Action as Business Leaders Gather at COP31
sg.description: ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Business and UN leaders gathered at COP31 today to address one of the most pressing challenges in global climate action: how to turn corporate commitments into measurable emissions reductions at a time of growing political uncertainty and economic pressure. Convened by the United Nations Global Compact, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) and UN Climate Change, the 14th Annual High-Level Meeting of Caring for Climate brought together chief executives and senior representatives from business, finance, Government, civil society and the United Nations to identify practical ways to accelerate climate action and overcome barriers that individual companies cannot tackle alone. The meeting came amid renewed warnings from UNEP that the world is on course to exceed 1.5°C of warming within the next few years. With the window for limiting the scale and duration of that overshoot narrowing, participants examined how businesses can sustain science-based climate ambition while translating transition plans into tangible results. "We meet at a defining moment for climate action. The magnitude and duration of the overshoot depends on the choices we make today, and returning to 1.5 degrees remains possible but only through urgent and sustained emissions reductions," said Sanda Ojiambo, UN Assistant Secretary-General, CEO and Executive Director of the UN Global Compact. "The next chapter of climate leadership will be defined not by the commitments we make but by the problems we solve, the emissions we cut and the clean, green energy transition that we deliver." Ms. Ojiambo stressed that many of the policies, technologies and solutions needed to accelerate climate action already exist. The challenge is deploying them at the speed and scale required. While corporate climate commitments have grown, implementation continues to lag, held back by policy uncertainty, inadequate infrastructure, financing constraints and continued fossil fuel subsidies. Building on the UN Secretary-General's engagement with business leaders at September's UN Private Sector Forum, where companies signalled their willingness to invest in the clean energy transition, the meeting focused on the conditions needed to turn that ambition into action across the wider economy. Discussions centred on three priorities: strengthening the credibility of corporate climate action, improving accountability for results and accelerating collective action to address systemic barriers. Participants examined how science-based targets and credible transition plans must be embedded in business strategy, operations and investment decisions, rather than treated as standalone sustainability commitments. They also explored the importance of transparent reporting, reliable data and measurable emissions reductions in demonstrating progress, identifying gaps and building confidence among investors, policymakers and other stakeholders. A central theme was that corporate ambition alone cannot deliver the transition. Clear and predictable government policies, investment in infrastructure and greater access to finance are essential to enable businesses to move faster, particularly in emerging and developing economies. Participants also considered how stronger collaboration between business, Governments, financial institutions and the United Nations can help overcome these obstacles. The meeting also considered how corporate climate leadership must extend beyond individual companies, including through responsible policy engagement, collaboration across value chains and support for the wider economic changes needed to achieve a just and resilient transition. Launched in 2007, Caring for Climate is a longstanding partnership between the UN Global Compact, UNEP and UN Climate Change to advance business leadership on climate action and strengthen dialogue between the private sector and policymakers. The High-Level Meeting is a centrepiece of the UN Global Compact's wider programme at COP31, which includes more than 20 sessions organized with its Country Networks on the clean energy transition, industrial decarbonization, circularity, climate resilience and a just transition. About Caring for Climate Launched in 2007, Caring for Climate is a partnership of the United Nations Global Compact, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and UN Climate Change (UNFCCC). It works to advance the role of business in addressing climate change by encouraging practical solutions, strengthening corporate climate leadership and supporting dialogue between business and policymakers. About the United Nations Global Compact As a special initiative of the United Nations Secretary-General, the UN Global Compact is a call to companies worldwide to align their operations and strategies with Ten Principles in the areas of human rights, labour, environment and anti-corruption. Our vision is clear: to mobilize business to transform sustainability ambition into action at the scale the world demands. With more than 25,000 participants and a presence in over 100 countries through 5 Regional Hubs and more than 70 Country Networks and expansion territories, the UN Global Compact is the world's largest corporate sustainability initiative. For more information, follow @globalcompact on social media and visit the UN Global Compact website.

id.description: Ringkasan Nintendo dan LEGO telah mengonfirmasi set Super Mario Yoshi baru yang dirancang khusus untuk para kolektor dewasaSempat dibocorkan di aplikasi Nintendo Today, rakitan mendatang ini menampilkan rekreasi pahatan wajah Yoshi dalam skala besarJumlah kepingan resmi, harga, dan jadwal peluncuran masih belum diumumkan menjelang indikasi kehadirannya pada tahun 2027 Raksasa produsen mainan LEGO dan perusahaan gim Nintendo secara resmi mengumumkan set LEGO Super Mario Yoshi terbaru yang dirancang khusus untuk para kolektor dewasa. Pertama kali dibocorkan melalui aplikasi seluler Nintendo Today dengan slogan "New Lego Super Mario Set Hatching Soon," perilisan mendatang ini akan memperluas katalog kolaboratif dengan kreasi ulang berbahan dasar balok yang mendetail dari dinosaurus hijau yang ikonis tersebut. Menjadi bagian dari koleksi khusus LEGO, "Adults Welcome", gambar *teaser* awal ini memberikan tampilan *close-up* wajah Yoshi, yang menampilkan mata yang terbuat dari balok, pipi tembem, dan hidung besar. Bentuknya yang terlihat mengindikasikan model berorientasi pajangan yang jauh lebih besar jika dibandingkan dengan figur interaktif yang lebih kecil yang menjadi standar pada rangkaian Super Mario utama. Meskipun detail mengenai apakah karakter tersebut akan hadir sebagai patung independen atau dengan aksesori seperti *kart* pribadinya masih belum dikonfirmasi, perilisan ini akan bergabung dengan karya utama Nintendo yang ditargetkan untuk orang dewasa seperti rakitan Mighty Bowser dan Piranha Plant. Set yang akan datang ini merupakan perilisan besar pertama Yoshi untuk orang dewasa sejak penghormatan terhadap seni piksel Super Mario World: Mario & Yoshi pada tahun 2024 yang berisi 1.215 bagian. Walau LEGO dan Nintendo belum mengonfirmasi harga resmi, jumlah bagian, atau tanggal perilisannya, pemberitahuan hak cipta tahun 2027 yang terlihat pada *teaser* tersebut menunjukkan bahwa set tersebut akan dirilis pada tahun mendatang. ph.title: UN Global Compact Calls for Faster Climate Action as Business Leaders Gather at COP31
ph.description: ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Business and UN leaders gathered at COP31 today to address one of the most pressing challenges in global climate action: how to turn corporate commitments into measurable emissions reductions at a time of growing political uncertainty and economic pressure. Convened by the United Nations Global Compact, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) and UN Climate Change, the 14th Annual High-Level Meeting of Caring for Climate brought together chief executives and senior representatives from business, finance, Government, civil society and the United Nations to identify practical ways to accelerate climate action and overcome barriers that individual companies cannot tackle alone. The meeting came amid renewed warnings from UNEP that the world is on course to exceed 1.5°C of warming within the next few years. With the window for limiting the scale and duration of that overshoot narrowing, participants examined how businesses can sustain science-based climate ambition while translating transition plans into tangible results. "We meet at a defining moment for climate action. The magnitude and duration of the overshoot depends on the choices we make today, and returning to 1.5 degrees remains possible but only through urgent and sustained emissions reductions," said Sanda Ojiambo, UN Assistant Secretary-General, CEO and Executive Director of the UN Global Compact. "The next chapter of climate leadership will be defined not by the commitments we make but by the problems we solve, the emissions we cut and the clean, green energy transition that we deliver." Ms. Ojiambo stressed that many of the policies, technologies and solutions needed to accelerate climate action already exist. The challenge is deploying them at the speed and scale required. While corporate climate commitments have grown, implementation continues to lag, held back by policy uncertainty, inadequate infrastructure, financing constraints and continued fossil fuel subsidies. Building on the UN Secretary-General's engagement with business leaders at September's UN Private Sector Forum, where companies signalled their willingness to invest in the clean energy transition, the meeting focused on the conditions needed to turn that ambition into action across the wider economy. Discussions centred on three priorities: strengthening the credibility of corporate climate action, improving accountability for results and accelerating collective action to address systemic barriers. Participants examined how science-based targets and credible transition plans must be embedded in business strategy, operations and investment decisions, rather than treated as standalone sustainability commitments. They also explored the importance of transparent reporting, reliable data and measurable emissions reductions in demonstrating progress, identifying gaps and building confidence among investors, policymakers and other stakeholders. A central theme was that corporate ambition alone cannot deliver the transition. Clear and predictable government policies, investment in infrastructure and greater access to finance are essential to enable businesses to move faster, particularly in emerging and developing economies. Participants also considered how stronger collaboration between business, Governments, financial institutions and the United Nations can help overcome these obstacles. The meeting also considered how corporate climate leadership must extend beyond individual companies, including through responsible policy engagement, collaboration across value chains and support for the wider economic changes needed to achieve a just and resilient transition. Launched in 2007, Caring for Climate is a longstanding partnership between the UN Global Compact, UNEP and UN Climate Change to advance business leadership on climate action and strengthen dialogue between the private sector and policymakers. The High-Level Meeting is a centrepiece of the UN Global Compact's wider programme at COP31, which includes more than 20 sessions organized with its Country Networks on the clean energy transition, industrial decarbonization, circularity, climate resilience and a just transition. About Caring for Climate Launched in 2007, Caring for Climate is a partnership of the United Nations Global Compact, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and UN Climate Change (UNFCCC). It works to advance the role of business in addressing climate change by encouraging practical solutions, strengthening corporate climate leadership and supporting dialogue between business and policymakers. About the United Nations Global Compact As a special initiative of the United Nations Secretary-General, the UN Global Compact is a call to companies worldwide to align their operations and strategies with Ten Principles in the areas of human rights, labour, environment and anti-corruption. Our vision is clear: to mobilize business to transform sustainability ambition into action at the scale the world demands. With more than 25,000 participants and a presence in over 100 countries through 5 Regional Hubs and more than 70 Country Networks and expansion territories, the UN Global Compact is the world's largest corporate sustainability initiative. For more information, follow @globalcompact on social media and visit the UN Global Compact website.

ph.title: Le Méridien Saigon Celebrates a Dynamic Year of Achievements, Innovation and Sustainability Milestones
ph.description: From the unveiling of its newly enhanced Ballroom to achieving Travelife Sustainability Certification, the hotel continues to elevate guest experiences while advancing its commitment to responsible hospitality. HO CHI MINH CITY, Vietnam, Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Le Méridien Saigon looks back on a dynamic year marked by meaningful achievements, continuous innovation and significant progress in its hospitality journey. From enhancing its event facilities to strengthening its sustainability commitments, the hotel continues to invest in delivering memorable experiences while setting new benchmarks for contemporary hospitality. Stylish suite design with river view of Le Méridien Saigon Elevating Event Experiences with a Newly Enhanced Ballroom A key highlight of the year is the official launch of Le Méridien Saigon's newly enhanced Ballroom, marking an important step in the hotel's ongoing commitment to elevating its event offerings. Designed to meet the evolving expectations of today's event planners and guests, the upgraded Ballroom brings together contemporary design and advanced audiovisual technology to create a more immersive, versatile and sophisticated event environment. The renovation introduces an integrated suite of next-generation technical features, including a ceiling-integrated 360-degree sound system with built-in subwoofers, PAR LED and Moving Beam lighting, and a 10-panel modular Dynamic LED system. These enhancements allow the space to adapt seamlessly to different event concepts, creating distinctive settings tailored to each occasion. Since officially opening its doors, the new Ballroom has received encouraging feedback from clients, particularly for its enhanced technical capabilities, versatile event configurations and the overall quality of service delivered by the hotel's dedicated team. These positive responses further reinforce Le Méridien Saigon's commitment to creating exceptional event experiences through the thoughtful combination of modern facilities, personalized service and meticulous attention to detail. From corporate conferences, exhibitions and product launches to elegant gala dinners, year-end celebrations and bespoke wedding receptions, the Ballroom offers a sophisticated setting for events of varying scales and styles. Advancing Responsible Hospitality with Travelife Certification Beyond enhancing its facilities and guest experiences, Le Méridien Saigon continues to make meaningful strides in its sustainability journey, achieving Travelife Sustainability Certification as another notable milestone this year. Travelife is an internationally recognized sustainability certification programme for the travel and hospitality industry, assessing accommodation providers against comprehensive criteria covering environmental management, social responsibility and sustainable business practices. This recognition reflects the hotel's ongoing efforts to integrate responsible practices into its daily operations, from promoting resource efficiency and responsible consumption to strengthening environmental awareness and fostering a culture of sustainability among its associates and partners. More than a recognition, the certification represents an ongoing commitment to making thoughtful choices that contribute to a more sustainable future for hospitality. Travelife certificate 2026 for Le Méridien Saigon Moving Forward with Purpose As Le Méridien Saigon reflects on a year of progress and achievements, these milestones represent more than individual accomplishments. They embody the hotel's continued dedication to evolving with the needs of its guests, creating meaningful experiences and embracing responsible business practices. Looking ahead, Le Méridien Saigon remains committed to pursuing new opportunities for innovation, service excellence and sustainable development, further enriching its position as a distinctive hospitality destination in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City. ph.title: Palace: P22.9-billion ASEAN hosting budget is ‘money well spent’
ph.description: Malacañang defended the government’s P22.9-billion allocation for hosting the 2026 Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and related meetings, describing the expenditure as an investment for the country and Filipino workers. Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro said this after BAYAN President Renato Reyes claimed that the public was being made to “suffer” because of what he described as the President’s “vanity” over the country’s preparations for the summit. In a press briefing on Thursday, Nov. 12, Castro rejected the accusation, saying the preparations were not intended for President Marcos. “To suffer? Because of the vanity of the President? Bakit ang Pangulo ba ang nagpapaganda sa sarili niya (Is the President beautifying himself)?” she said. “Ano ba ang pinapaganda natin—hindi ba ang Pilipinas (What are we improving, if not the Philippines)?” she added. According to the Palace Press Officer, the preparations were intended to present the Philippines as a country where foreign investors could confidently place their investments. “Anong gusto nilang makita sa ating bansa, isang maduming bansa (What do they want to see in our country, a dirty country)?” she said. “Huwag ipahid kay Pangulo ang lahat ng mga pagbibintang nila nang walang anumang basehan. Hindi mismo ang Pangulo ang nagpapaganda sa sarili niya, ang pinapaganda niya ay bansa at ang kapakanan ng bawat Pilipino (Do not pin all their accusations on the President without any basis. The President is not beautifying himself; what he is improving is the country and the welfare of every Filipino),” she added. Castro said the P22.9-billion allocation was justified by the scale of preparations, the opportunities for local industries, and the potential economic and security benefits the Philippines could gain from hosting the regional gatherings. “The peso na magagastos natin ay investment para sa ating bansa at para sa ating mga Pilipino at Pilipinong manggagawa (Every peso that we spend is an investment for our country, our Filipino people, and Filipino workers),” she said. She stressed, however, that the P22.9 billion represented the total funding allocated for ASEAN 2026 and not the amount already spent, adding that the government could provide a final accounting only after the summit and related activities were completed. Castro said the government was prepared to report the expenditures and submit them to Commission on Audit (COA) scrutiny, emphasizing the administration’s commitment to preventing corruption. Government cites scale of preparations Castro said the preparations covered two major hosting milestones, the May 8 to 9 ASEAN meetings in Cebu and the November 2026 summit in Metro Manila. Among the projects she cited were improvements to the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC), which will serve as the principal venue for the November summit, the Coconut Palace, the World Trade Center, and infrastructure in Cebu. She also cited airport improvements, including general-aviation facilities, aircraft aprons, airport road lighting, and VIP lounges. For security, the government will deploy 22,944 police personnel—nearly 20,000 from the National Capital Region—with support from the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), the Presidential Security Command (PSC), and the Highway Patrol Group (HPG). The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) will also deploy more than 1,000 personnel for traffic management, while security and emergency resources will include patrol vehicles, ambulances, K-9 units, tactical watercraft, trucks, and buses. Economic, diplomatic benefits Castro said the hosting was not merely an event but an opportunity to strengthen partnerships and advance Philippine national interests in the region. She cited potential benefits such as more jobs and business opportunities, safer digital transactions, and greater energy security, as well as the proposed ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement and the ASEAN-Canada Free Trade Agreement, which she said could expand market access for Philippine exporters and service providers. The Palace official also pointed to the volume of diplomatic engagements, saying the government had completed 393 meetings to advance its priorities and had another 164 scheduled, bringing the total to more than 550 meetings. She compared this with the 279 meetings held during the Philippines’ 2017 ASEAN chairship, arguing that the scale and outcomes of the hosting should be considered alongside its cost. In his Nov. 12 vlog, President Marcos likewise said the Philippines would use its chairship to prioritize concerns such as oil and food prices, security, agriculture, jobs, and livelihoods, noting that many regional problems could not be addressed by countries acting alone. Palace defends summit-related preparations Meanwhile, Castro defended the installation of barriers and coverings along waterways beside roads leading to airports, saying these were part of security measures and included displays of artwork by Filipino artists. “Parte ito ng seguridad at…sa aking nakita, mayroon tayong nakitang mga arts na ginawa (This was part of security measures, and, from what I saw, there were artworks there),” she said. “Ito ay pagmamalaki na rin kung ano ang kakayahan ng mga kinikilala nating mga artist sa Pilipinas (This is also our way of showing pride in the skills of Filipino artists),” she added. She rejected criticism that the preparations were being undertaken for the President’s vanity, saying the government was presenting the country as a place where foreign investors could confidently do business.

bd.title: UN Global Compact Calls for Faster Climate Action as Business Leaders Gather at COP31
bd.description: ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Business and UN leaders gathered at COP31 today to address one of the most pressing challenges in global climate action: how to turn corporate commitments into measurable emissions reductions at a time of growing political uncertainty and economic pressure. Convened by the United Nations Global Compact, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) and UN Climate Change, the 14th Annual High-Level Meeting of Caring for Climate brought together chief executives and senior representatives from business, finance, Government, civil society and the United Nations to identify practical ways to accelerate climate action and overcome barriers that individual companies cannot tackle alone. The meeting came amid renewed warnings from UNEP that the world is on course to exceed 1.5°C of warming within the next few years. With the window for limiting the scale and duration of that overshoot narrowing, participants examined how businesses can sustain science-based climate ambition while translating transition plans into tangible results. "We meet at a defining moment for climate action. The magnitude and duration of the overshoot depends on the choices we make today, and returning to 1.5 degrees remains possible but only through urgent and sustained emissions reductions," said Sanda Ojiambo, UN Assistant Secretary-General, CEO and Executive Director of the UN Global Compact. "The next chapter of climate leadership will be defined not by the commitments we make but by the problems we solve, the emissions we cut and the clean, green energy transition that we deliver." Ms. Ojiambo stressed that many of the policies, technologies and solutions needed to accelerate climate action already exist. The challenge is deploying them at the speed and scale required. While corporate climate commitments have grown, implementation continues to lag, held back by policy uncertainty, inadequate infrastructure, financing constraints and continued fossil fuel subsidies. Building on the UN Secretary-General's engagement with business leaders at September's UN Private Sector Forum, where companies signalled their willingness to invest in the clean energy transition, the meeting focused on the conditions needed to turn that ambition into action across the wider economy. Discussions centred on three priorities: strengthening the credibility of corporate climate action, improving accountability for results and accelerating collective action to address systemic barriers. Participants examined how science-based targets and credible transition plans must be embedded in business strategy, operations and investment decisions, rather than treated as standalone sustainability commitments. They also explored the importance of transparent reporting, reliable data and measurable emissions reductions in demonstrating progress, identifying gaps and building confidence among investors, policymakers and other stakeholders. A central theme was that corporate ambition alone cannot deliver the transition. Clear and predictable government policies, investment in infrastructure and greater access to finance are essential to enable businesses to move faster, particularly in emerging and developing economies. Participants also considered how stronger collaboration between business, Governments, financial institutions and the United Nations can help overcome these obstacles. The meeting also considered how corporate climate leadership must extend beyond individual companies, including through responsible policy engagement, collaboration across value chains and support for the wider economic changes needed to achieve a just and resilient transition. Launched in 2007, Caring for Climate is a longstanding partnership between the UN Global Compact, UNEP and UN Climate Change to advance business leadership on climate action and strengthen dialogue between the private sector and policymakers. The High-Level Meeting is a centrepiece of the UN Global Compact's wider programme at COP31, which includes more than 20 sessions organized with its Country Networks on the clean energy transition, industrial decarbonization, circularity, climate resilience and a just transition. About Caring for Climate Launched in 2007, Caring for Climate is a partnership of the United Nations Global Compact, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and UN Climate Change (UNFCCC). It works to advance the role of business in addressing climate change by encouraging practical solutions, strengthening corporate climate leadership and supporting dialogue between business and policymakers. About the United Nations Global Compact As a special initiative of the United Nations Secretary-General, the UN Global Compact is a call to companies worldwide to align their operations and strategies with Ten Principles in the areas of human rights, labour, environment and anti-corruption. Our vision is clear: to mobilize business to transform sustainability ambition into action at the scale the world demands. With more than 25,000 participants and a presence in over 100 countries through 5 Regional Hubs and more than 70 Country Networks and expansion territories, the UN Global Compact is the world's largest corporate sustainability initiative. From corporate conferences, exhibitions and product launches to elegant gala dinners, year-end celebrations and bespoke wedding receptions, the Ballroom offers a sophisticated setting for events of varying scales and styles. Advancing Responsible Hospitality with Travelife Certification Beyond enhancing its facilities and guest experiences, Le Méridien Saigon continues to make meaningful strides in its sustainability journey, achieving Travelife Sustainability Certification as another notable milestone this year. Travelife is an internationally recognized sustainability certification programme for the travel and hospitality industry, assessing accommodation providers against comprehensive criteria covering environmental management, social responsibility and sustainable business practices. This recognition reflects the hotel's ongoing efforts to integrate responsible practices into its daily operations, from promoting resource efficiency and responsible consumption to strengthening environmental awareness and fostering a culture of sustainability among its associates and partners. More than a recognition, the certification represents an ongoing commitment to making thoughtful choices that contribute to a more sustainable future for hospitality. From enhancing its event facilities to strengthening its sustainability commitments, the hotel continues to invest in delivering memorable experiences while setting new benchmarks for contemporary hospitality. Designed to meet the evolving expectations of today's event planners and guests, the upgraded Ballroom brings together contemporary design and advanced audiovisual technology to create a more immersive, versatile and sophisticated event environment. The renovation introduces an integrated suite of next-generation technical features, including a ceiling-integrated 360-degree sound system with built-in subwoofers, PAR LED and Moving Beam lighting, and a 10-panel modular Dynamic LED system. These enhancements allow the space to adapt seamlessly to different event concepts, creating distinctive settings tailored to each occasion. Since officially opening its doors, the new Ballroom has received encouraging feedback from clients, particularly for its enhanced technical capabilities, versatile event configurations and the overall quality of service delivered by the hotel's dedicated team. From corporate conferences, exhibitions and product launches to elegant gala dinners, year-end celebrations and bespoke wedding receptions, the Ballroom offers a sophisticated setting for events of varying scales and styles. Advancing Responsible Hospitality with Travelife Certification Beyond enhancing its facilities and guest experiences, Le Méridien Saigon continues to make meaningful strides in its sustainability journey, achieving Travelife Sustainability Certification as another notable milestone this year. Travelife is an internationally recognized sustainability certification programme for the travel and hospitality industry, assessing accommodation providers against comprehensive criteria covering environmental management, social responsibility and sustainable business practices. This recognition reflects the hotel's ongoing efforts to integrate responsible practices into its daily operations, from promoting resource efficiency and responsible consumption to strengthening environmental awareness and fostering a culture of sustainability among its associates and partners. More than a recognition, the certification represents an ongoing commitment to making thoughtful choices that contribute to a more sustainable future for hospitality. They embody the hotel's continued dedication to evolving with the needs of its guests, creating meaningful experiences and embracing responsible business practices. Looking ahead, Le Méridien Saigon remains committed to pursuing new opportunities for innovation, service excellence and sustainable development, further enriching its position as a distinctive hospitality destination in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City. iq.description: شفق نيوز- دمشق عادت قرابة 400 عائلة من مهجري منطقة رأس العين "سري كانيه" من قاطني مخيم واشوكاني في الحسكة إلى مناطقهم الأصلية ضمن القافلة الثامنة، اليوم الخميس. وقال المتحدث باسم لجنة مهجري سري كانيه، محمود جميل لوكالة شفق نيوز إنه "بعد الانتهاء من الإجراءات اللوجستية والتنسيق بين قوى الأمن الداخلي والوفد الرئاسي ومفوضية اللاجئين انطلقت صباح اليوم 375 عائلة مهجرة من مخيم واشوكاني وعدد من مراكز الإيواء (المدارس)". وأوضح إن "العوائل العائدة إلى مناطقها الاصلية تنحدر من مناطق ريف سري كانيه ومنطقة زركان وريف تل تمر شمال الحسكة". وجدد جمل، دعوته لمنظمات الأمم المتحدة والجهات المعنية العمل على زيادة عدد العوائل في كل قافلة وتسريع آلية إعادة النازحين بشكل طوحي وآمن إلى مناطقهم الاصلية في سري كانيه وريفها". يُذكر أن سبعة قوافل للعودة نُظمت منذ آب الماضي وحتى الآن، وشملت عودة أكثر من 4100 عائلة إلى رأس العين "سري كانيه" وأريافها، فضلاً عن عدد من القرى في أرياف تل تمر وزركان وأبو راسين شمالي الحسكة. وتسببت العملية العسكرية التركية، بمشاركة فصائل سورية معارضة، والتي أُطلق عليها اسم "نبع السلام" عام 2019، بنزوح قرابة 300 ألف شخص من منطقتي رأس العين وتل أبيض، خلال الأيام الأولى للهجوم، وفق تقارير أممية وحقوقية.

za.title: Mbappe ruled out of France's Nations League game against Italy
za.description: Mbappe ruled out of France's Nations League game against Italy Estelle. Bronkhorst Thu, 11/12/2026 - 10:30 MILAN - France's captain Kylian Mbappe will miss his country's Nations League match against Italy with a hamstring problem, coach Zinedine Zidane said Wednesday. Les Bleus take on Roberto Mancini's Italy in Milan on Thursday as they bid to strengthen their grip on top spot in Group A1, before facing Turkey in Bordeaux on Sunday. "He will miss tomorrow, he felt a little pain and we won't take any risk," said Zidane. "It's a shame to lose players but it's part of the game. I hope that it's nothing too serious and that he'll be available for Sunday... It's just a minor issue." The Real Madrid forward is back in the France squad for this camp after missing their last three matches through injury. He has already netted 17 goals in all competitions for his club this season. Mbappe scored the winning goal in Zidane's first match as coach, against Turkey in September in the Nations League, but had to leave the pitch shortly afterwards due to pain in his left knee. After three wins and a draw in four group games, victory over Italy would see France qualify for the quarter-finals. AFP

za.title: Sunken treasure: Historic US ocean liner reborn as artifical reef
za.description: Sunken treasure: Historic US ocean liner reborn as artifical reef Estelle. Bronkhorst Thu, 11/12/2026 - 10:30 MIAMI - A majestic and all-but-indestructible 20th-century ocean liner that once ferried royal leaders, movie stars and even the "Mona Lisa" to the United States was being deliberately sunk to become the world's largest artificial reef. Experts were conducting a controlled flood-sink of the 302-metre vessel, a veteran of more than 800 transatlantic crossings in the 1950s and 60s, that is set to send it to its final resting place on the Gulf of Mexico's sandy floor, some 40 kilometres southwest of Destin-Fort Walton Beach, Florida. "Two of the valves have been opened. The deployment process has started," said an official on the livestream operated by the city. Florida's Okaloosa County, gambling that such a huge new reef would be a local tourism boom and attract dive and fishing enthusiasts, bought the long-decommissioned SS United States from a conservancy group for $1 million in 2024. The vessel -- longer than the Titanic and the transatlantic speed record holder -- will become the centrepiece of Okaloosa's undersea garden of sunken ships, including World War II vessels, tugboats, and even a casino boat. Captain Tim Mullane of Alabama-based maritime company Coleen Marine which led the repurposing, has described it as "a great honour to put this fine vessel to rest... where it's going to serve a second life" promoting marine fauna, diving and fishing. A year-long process of cleaning the vessel, removing all toxins like fuel, paint and wiring, towing, environmental remediation, safety assurances, and eventual sinking cost roughly $13.5 million. The SS United States, the result of a celebrated feat of mid-century American engineering, made its maiden voyage in 1952. In its heyday, the luxury liner carried countless celebrities, including president John F Kennedy, Former King Edward VIII, Grace Kelly, Elizabeth Taylor and Salvador Dali. Future president Bill Clinton travelled on board on his way to study at Oxford. Perhaps its most famous passenger was Leonardo de Vinci's "Mona Lisa," the 16th-century painting that visited America in 1963. Within two decades of being built, the liner was out of service, falling victim to the growing popularity of air travel. It remained docked in Philadelphia for 29 years. While the ship will rest at a depth of 180 feet, its top decks will be just about 55 feet below the water's surface, reachable for beginner divers. Until now, the largest artificial reef was an aircraft carrier sunk 20 years ago off the coast of Pensacola, also in Florida. Repurposing the SS United States keeps its heritage alive, said Okaloosa County tourism director Jennifer Adams Kemp. "She's our country's flagship," she told CNN shortly before the sinking. "Why wouldn't we want to preserve that?" AFP

za.title: Uganda: Sustainable financing of new cities key to development - Member of Parliament (MP) Alobo
za.description: Government should provide adequate, predictable and sustainable financing for cities, and ring-fence domestic budgetary allocations for roads, drainages, markets, waste management and other critical urban infrastructure. The call was contained in a motion moved by Soroti City Woman Representative, Hon. Joan Alobo who urged government to prioritise development and financing of cities in Uganda as engines of socio-economic transformation. In the motion presented on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, Alobo noted that 10 out of 15 cities including Arua, Gulu, Lira, Soroti, Mbale, Jinja, Masaka, Mbarara, Fort Portal and Hoima have been operationalised. She added that the proposed cities of Kabale, Moroto, Nakasongola, Entebbe and Wakiso are yet to become functional. “The 10 cities are operating well below their approved staffing structures, most of them lack approved physical development plans, statutory bodies such as City Service Commissions are grossly underfunded and the regulations required to guide city governance have not been issued,” Alobo said. She observed that on 31 March 2026, the World Bank approved US$540 million in International Development Association financing for the six-year Uganda Cities and Municipalities Infrastructure Development (UCMID) programme covering 10 cities, 26 municipalities and 13 refugee-hosting districts. The funding is expected to benefit approximately 5.6 million people including 600,000 refugees and create up to 40,000 direct jobs through climate-smart infrastructure and local economic development. “Let it be resolved by this Parliament that government aligns and coordinates with World Bank, African Development Bank and other development-partner investments within the National Cities Development and Investment Strategy, while ensuring complementarity, timely counterpart funding and measurable regional outcomes,” Alobo said. She, however, noted that donor money alone cannot build cities adding that without a national strategy, predictable domestic financing and clear targets, such investments will be scattered and their impact short-lived. “Government should prepare and submit to Parliament, within six months of the adoption of this resolution, a costed and time-bound implementation framework for the National Cities Development and Investment Strategy, indicating annual budgetary commitments, development-partner financing, responsible Ministries, Departments and Agencies and measurable outcomes,” Alobo proposed. Hon. Martin Ojara (NRM, Bardege-Layibi Division) observing that several parishes and sub-counties that were merged with municipalities to meet the threshold of a city status have received the much-required services. “Many of those sub-counties that became part of the cities lack electricity, piped-water lines and struggle to have access to roads. There is need to provide adequate funding to enable the annexed areas get the services that a city is entitled to,” Mapenduzi said. Hon. Denis Alyela (NRM, Lira East Division) noted that the concentration of economic activities, specialised services and investment opportunities in Kampala has placed enormous pressure on the capital city through rural-urban migration. He suggested deliberate investment in regional cities to distribute economic opportunities, promote local industry and strengthen the agricultural value chain. “A city should not merely be a change of name or administrative status, but must represent transformation in infrastructure, service delivery, economic opportunities and the quality of life of our people,” Alyela said. Hoima West Division MP, Hon. Ismail Kasule cited the case of Hoima City that lacks a city hospital, proper road network and proper waste management, which he attributed to insufficient and unpredictable financing for city authorities. “In Hoima City, we have 16 wards but only two have reached 60 per cent of electricity connection. These cities annexed many wards from other divisions of the district and thus need to be prioritised to enable their development,” Kasule said. Mbarara City Woman Representative, Hon. Charity Kibaaju called on government to establish a dedicated financing window to prioritise waste management, secondary drainage channels and restoration of urban river banks. The State Minister for Urban Development, Hon. Margaret Muhanga said urban opportunities are immense and should be harnessed through deliberate interventions, adding that new cities must not be merely created, but should work as engines of economic development. “We need to complete all the necessary legal policy frameworks for city development and management, build on the completed regulatory assessment and review the National Urban Policy of 2017,” she added. The Government Chief Whip, Hon. Jane Ruth Aceng emphasised the need for MPs to supervise the operations of cities to ensure value for money, particularly on the UCMID programme. Distributed by APO Group on behalf of Parliament of the Republic of Uganda.
